newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Main shareholders to reduce Tricom stake.
newsitem.headline: Main shareholders to reduce Tricom stake.

text.p: Tricom Holdings Ltd's 67.89 percent controlling shareholders might cut their stake in the company to raise the public shareholding to the stock exchange prescribed minimum 25 percent level, Tricom said on Thursday.

"The company is now considering various ways to restore the prescribed minimum percentage of securities in public hands, including a possible proportional sell-down of shares held by the controlling shareholders to independent investors," Tricom said in a statement.

Tricom said the public shareholding fell to 21.08 percent from 32.1 percent after Rockie Investment Co Ltd bought 2.52 million shares which raised its stake in the company to 11.03 percent from 9.9 percent.
Rockie Investment is controlled by Joseph Tsui, a former director of Tricom.
Shares of the telecommunications products supplier ended unchanged at HK$0.80 each on Wednesday.
